title: Stated Detail
summary: The answer is in the text. Go back to the right spot before reading the choices, then pick the faithful paraphrase.

slides.title: Look it up, don’t remember it
body: Detail questions ask what the passage says. The answer is a paraphrase of a specific line, so the winning move is to find that line before you read the choices.
Wrong answers use the passage’s words in the wrong combination: right names, wrong relationship.
slides.callout: Go to the text first. A choice that only sounds familiar is the trap.

slides.title: How you’ll see it
stems: Which one of the following is mentioned in the passage as …?
The author explicitly identifies which one of the following?

steps.label: Find the spot
steps.do: Use your paragraph map to go straight to the relevant lines.

steps.label: Reread with neighbours
steps.do: Read the sentence plus the one before and after.

steps.label: Predict
steps.do: Put what it says in your own words.

steps.label: Match exactly
steps.do: Choose the paraphrase. Reject choices that mix up who did what, or add a detail.

slides.title: Worked example

paragraphs: The letters of the eighteenth-century merchant Ottilie Brandt survive in two collections. The larger, held in Bremen, contains her business correspondence; the smaller, in Riga, contains letters to her sister.

Historians long relied on the Bremen letters alone and portrayed Brandt as a cautious trader who avoided risky ventures. The Riga letters, catalogued only in 1998, complicate that picture: in them Brandt describes financing two voyages to the West Indies through a partner, an arrangement that appears nowhere in her business correspondence.

slides.stem: According to the passage, the Riga letters

choices.A: were written to Brandt by her sister
choices.B: describe ventures that are not mentioned in Brandt's business correspondence
choices.C: show that Brandt lost money on voyages to the West Indies
choices.D: make up the larger of the two collections
choices.E: were catalogued before historians began describing Brandt as a cautious trader who avoided risk

steps.label: Find the spot
steps.note: Riga is described in both paragraphs. Paragraph 2 says what the letters contain.
steps.highlight: an arrangement that appears nowhere in her business correspondence

steps.label: Predict
steps.note: The Riga letters mention voyages that the business letters leave out.

why.A: Reversed: the letters are to her sister, not from her.
why.B: Correct. A direct paraphrase of the final sentence.
why.C: Profit or loss is never mentioned.
why.D: The Bremen collection is the larger one.
why.E: Historians relied on the Bremen letters, and the Riga letters were catalogued only in 1998, so this has the order backwards.

slides.title: Cheat card
lines: Go back to the text before the choices.
Read the sentence with its neighbours.
Right words, wrong relationship is the usual trap.
Nothing extra: no profit, motive or date the text didn’t give.
